items.prompt: In a non-empty array every element appears twice except for one. Find that one in O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
items.why: 'Twice except one' + O(1) space → XOR fold: x ^ x = 0 cancels every pair. A counter is O(n) space, and sorting is O(n log n).

items.prompt: Exactly two elements appear once and all others appear twice. Return the two singles in O(n) time and O(1) space.
items.why: The fold gives a ^ b; any set bit of it splits the array into two groups, each with one single → Bitwise XOR. There's no 1..n range for cyclic sort.

items.prompt: Given a positive integer, return the number you get by flipping every bit of its binary representation (no leading zeros).
items.why: 'Flip every bit' → XOR with a mask of all 1s as wide as the number. Building a binary string, flipping characters and parsing it back works, but it is the slow, clunky route.

items.prompt: Every element appears three times except one, which appears once. Find the single element in O(n) time and O(1) space.
items.why: XOR cancels pairs, not triples → count each bit column modulo 3 (general Bit Manipulation). A counter breaks the O(1) space limit.

items.prompt: An array of length n holds values in 1..n; several values are missing and several are repeated. Return all the missing values in O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
items.why: Several unknowns → the XOR fold mixes them into one number. Values in 1..n with mutation allowed → Cyclic Sort, then scan.

items.prompt: String t is string s shuffled, with one extra letter added. Return the extra letter.
items.why: Two collections that match except for one item → XOR all character codes of both, and the extra one survives. A counter works, but it costs a map.

items.prompt: Return the k most frequent elements of an integer array.
items.why: Arbitrary frequencies, and the k largest by count → Top 'K' Elements (count, then a heap of size k). XOR only tells you about odd versus even counts.
